claims.text: HfNbTiVAl10 has a reported hierarchical heterostructure with multilevel chemical fluctuations.
A limited set of targeted ab initio and CALPHAD calculations can be used to calibrate a machine-learning interatomic potential representing relevant local chemical environments.
Surrogate interatomic-potential simulations can be coupled to a continuum or phase-field model to represent the larger-scale heterogeneity of HfNbTiVAl10.
The hierarchical microstructure can be represented by effective mesoscopic descriptors that connect localized atomic interactions to macroscopic mechanical response.
A surrogate potential can rapidly predict local elastic stiffness and deformation behavior.
The surrogate potential can predict local yielding behavior and crack-tip stress distributions accurately enough for bulk-property prediction.
A mesoscale model can aggregate local responses over heterostructured domains to obtain bulk Young's modulus, yield strength, and fracture toughness.
Replacing extensive high-fidelity calculations with a calibrated surrogate can reduce computational cost.
The proposed framework will predict Young's modulus of hierarchical-heterostructured HfNbTiVAl10 within ±10% of experiment.
The proposed framework will predict yield strength of hierarchical-heterostructured HfNbTiVAl10 within ±10% of experiment.
The proposed framework will predict fracture toughness of hierarchical-heterostructured HfNbTiVAl10 within ±10% of experiment.
The proposed framework will provide an approximately 10× computational-efficiency improvement over full ab initio/CALPHAD approaches.
Traditional high-fidelity thermodynamic and first-principles workflows incur substantial computational costs.
Existing approaches struggle to predict fracture toughness reliably.
The framework is expected to remain applicable only while the tested heterostructure and chemical fluctuations are stable and represented by the training data.
Unrepresented phase transformations, unexpected segregation, or poorly sampled local environments can undermine surrogate-model accuracy.
The accuracy and efficiency estimates depend on training-data representativeness and on the fidelity of the mesoscale heterostructure model.
The proposed benchmark compares independently generated predictions with tensile and fracture measurements made under identical testing conditions and records CPU or GPU usage.
The hypothesis is declared falsified if any predicted property differs from experiment by more than 15% or if computational cost is reduced by less than 5×.

contradictions.description: The claimed accuracy is within ±10%, but the benchmark falsifies only errors greater than ±15%. Results between 10% and 15% would violate the prediction without falsifying the hypothesis.
The claimed efficiency gain is approximately 10×, but the benchmark falsifies only gains below 5×. A result from 5× to well below 10× would miss the claimed gain without falsifying the hypothesis.
